summary: Configured a secure, persistent SSH local tunnel from node2 127.0.0.1:9082 to node1 127.0.0.1:9081. It automatically recovers from SSH interruption and node restarts. Both application listeners remain inaccessible through cluster addresses, protected files are unchanged, and SELinux/firewalld remain active.
actions_performed: Added an enabled, hardened systemd service for the existing node1 status application.
Created a dedicated key-only, non-login SSH identity restricted to local forwarding solely to 127.0.0.1:9081.
Added and enabled inventory-ssh-tunnel.service on node2 with host-key pinning and automatic restart.
Verified allowed loopback behavior and denied non-loopback access from both nodes.
Demonstrated automatic tunnel recreation after terminating its dedicated SSH session.
Safely restarted node1 and node2 sequentially and verified changed boot identities and full recovery.
Confirmed RHEL 10.0 and kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0.x86_64 remained unchanged.

evidence.summary: The document is available through node2 loopback port 9082; ports 9081 and 9082 reject cluster-address access and listen only on their respective loopback addresses.
The destination account is key-only with PermitOpen limited to 127.0.0.1:9081; the tunnel service is enabled, active, host-key pinned, and runs SSH as the dedicated identity.
After terminating only the dedicated server-side SSH session, systemd increased its restart count, created a new SSH process, and restored the status endpoint automatically.

evidence.requirement: Protected application and status document preserved
evidence.summary: Pre-change and final SHA-256 hashes match for serve.py and status/index.html; the original ready document remains intact.
Shows healthy baseline, safe restart acknowledgement, boot ID change, recovered inventory/SSH services and unchanged data, plus dependent tunnel recovery.
Shows healthy baseline, safe restart acknowledgement, boot ID change, restored tunnel/SSH services, preserved credentials, successful HTTP behavior, and continued loopback-only exposure.
Both nodes have zero failed units; SELinux remains enforcing, firewalld active, configuration validates, administrative SSH remains active, and OS/kernel releases are unchanged.
